source.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
source.authors: Hunar Batra; Lachin Naghashyar; Ashkan Khakzar; P. Torr; Christian Schroeder de Witt; Constantin Venhoff; Ronald Clark

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE dictionaries recover task-related sparse features in multimodal LLMs, a setting beyond the toy models in the original superposition work. It does not test the toy-model superposition geometry itself.
record.gate_note: The paper motivates SAEs by superposition and says they mitigate it, but it does not test feature-over-capacity storage, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, feature-importance tradeoffs, or neuron polysemanticity. Rows record the paper's own SAE feature discovery, interventions, and dictionary-stability results. Excluded cited background claims, selection thresholds used to choose features, and attribution-patching plots that do not measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper uses SAEs as a tool, citing superposition only as motivation. Its results measure how well its own MMDiff pipeline finds and controls features in MLLMs: ablation effects, steering gains and selection-rule comparisons. It does not test whether features are superposed or spread across neurons, or whether SAE features are complete or canonical units. The seed and correspondence checks are warm-started from the same base SAE, so high alignment largely follows from the initialization. They validate index alignment for the method rather than test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that multimodal SAEs warm-started from base-LM dictionaries and diffed against them yield sparse, causally specific features. Ablating these features selectively degrades spatial and OCR performance and reduces ASR without VQA cost. Steering with them beats single-layer CAA. The authors also say cross-stage ablation suggests PaliGemma 2 mid-layer spatial features are mainly acquired during multimodal fine-tuning. They make no claim about superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: This is a multimodal SAE feature-discovery and intervention study, not a reproduction of Toy Models of Superposition. It uses learned dictionaries and feature ablation/steering in multimodal LLMs rather than toy-network feature-loading experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature recovery and selectivity depend on SAE warm-start/model diffing, text-only versus other token-mask training regimes, and the adapted-feature and lexical-invariance filters. The paper reports materially different results when selection rules or SAE initialization change.

fits_no_version.finding: A randomly initialized SAE trained directly on LLaVA-MORE activations yielded top spatial features that fire on 100% of VSR samples. Ablating them did not change VSR (mean +0.22, versus −10.11 for MMDiff features).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastive selection over from-scratch MLLM SAEs fails to isolate task-causal features, because always-on features saturate the odds ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: Warm-started SAEs retrained with a different seed and data order keep a mean same-index decoder cosine of about 0.93, with under 1% of features relocated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuned SAE dictionaries that share a warm start are reproducible across seeds.

record.problems: The study covers three MLLM families, but safety and OCR are evaluated on PaliGemma 2 only. The spatial feature evaluations use feature-specific subsets. The paper notes that a minority of safety candidates cause generation collapse and need post-hoc filtering. Seed-stability evidence is reported for selected PaliGemma 2 layers, not broadly across all models or dictionaries.
record.rows_left_out: Steering-method comparisons in Tables 3, 6, and 14 were left out because they primarily compare the proposed steering recipe with CAA baselines, rather than measuring the claimed superposition or feature-recovery property itself. Cross-stage ablations and attribution-patching results were also omitted because they concern training-stage effects or head localization rather than a claim version.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry or sparsity transitions.
No test of whether capacity competition drives polysemanticity.
No analysis of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Assumes superposition and SAE recovery, citing them. It measures no neuron-level spread and no recovery fidelity as evidence of sparse features.
Completeness, canonicity and stability across independently initialized dictionaries are untested. The seed checks share a warm start.
Uses 1-D decoder directions without comparing them to multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Four MMDiff-Qwen spatial features (L15/F18534 −17.14, L13/F8678 −16.95, L18/F16094 −16.75, L17/F9200 −14.82 ∆VSR) are absent from the rows. Only four of the eight Qwen features were recorded; the reported mean of −14.6 requires all eight.

record.verdict_notes: Superposition appears only as background motivation for using SAEs (App. A.2). The record's V4 and V5 links treat method validation as tests of the claim. Row ranges are grouped in row_fixes for brevity.

versions.untested_parts: No toy network or test of overlapping near-orthogonal feature geometry, sparsity transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Does not investigate non-capacity explanations for polysemantic neurons.
Does not establish that features are spread across neurons; SAE feature recovery and causal effects are tested only in the reported MLLMs, tasks, and intervention settings.
Tests dictionary alignment and seed stability in PaliGemma 2, but not feature completeness or canonical status across methods, models, or training runs.
Uses one-dimensional SAE decoder directions but does not compare them with multidimensional features or test whether superposition consists of 1-D directions.
